Snapshot of the CHANGELOG entry for v0.3.0, used as the GitHub Release body:
    gh release create v0.3.0 --title "Asuka 0.3.0" \
        --notes-file .github/release-notes/v0.3.0.md dist/*

---

## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-16

First release since 0.2.0. This is a large, partly breaking update: the
detector API, the packaging and the internal scanner all changed, and the
detector count grew from 9 to 18.

### Added

- Nine detectors (18 total):
  - `SWC-106` Unprotected Selfdestruct
  - `SWC-116` Timestamp Dependence
  - `SWC-120` Weak Sources of Randomness
  - `201` Unchecked Token Transfer (ERC20/721 `transfer` results discarded)
  - `202` Imprecise Arithmetic Order (`a / b * c`)
  - `203` Tautological Comparison (`x == x`)
  - `204` Right-To-Left-Override Character (bidi control characters)
  - `205` Deprecated Solidity Standards (`suicide`/`sha3`/`msg.gas`)
  - `206` Dangerous Unary Expression (`!x == y`, `~x > y`)
- The detector set is now: the nine above plus the detectors already available
  in 0.2.0 - `SWC-100` Function Default Visibility, `SWC-101` Int Overflow,
  `SWC-104` Unchecked Return Value, `SWC-107` Reentrancy, `SWC-109` Access of
  Uninitialized Pointer, `SWC-112` Delegatecall to Untrusted Callee,
  `SWC-115` Authorization through tx.origin, `137` Arbitrary calls and
  `138` msg.value in loop.
- Cross-file scanning: local imports (`"./x.sol"`, `"../lib/x.sol"`,
  `"/contracts/x.sol"`) are resolved into a project graph with a symbol table,
  so inheritance chains and declared types resolve across files. Imported
  files are resolution-only and never become scan targets.
- Inheritance-aware detectors: `reentrancy` and `unchecked-transfer` see state
  variables inherited from base contracts, including ones declared in another
  file.
- Error isolation: a file that fails to parse or crashes a detector no longer
  aborts the scan; failures are collected in `Asuka.errors` and reported by
  the CLI.
- Strict parsing mode: syntax errors fail a file explicitly instead of
  silently producing an empty AST.
- CLI warnings for local imports that cannot be found.
- Development tooling: `pyproject.toml` packaging, pytest suite (397 tests,
  98% coverage), ruff linting, GitHub Actions CI on Python 3.11–3.14,
  `AGENTS.md` repository guide, and documentation-consistency tests.

### Changed

- **Breaking** — detectors are now `Detector` subclasses registered in
  `vuls/all_detector.py`, instead of modules exposing `NAME`/`ID`/`check()`.
  Results are built with `self.result(vul_list)`.
- **Breaking** — `Vuls.descreibe` renamed to `Vuls.description`; the detector
  constants `DESCREIBE`/`METHED` became `DESCRIPTION`/`METHODS`.
- **Breaking** — packaging moved from `setup.py` + `requirements.txt` to
  `pyproject.toml`; the `asuka` console script is unchanged.
- Python 3.11+ is now required (was 3.9-era code that also failed on 3.13+).
- Type annotations across all hand-written modules; ruff `UP` rules enabled
  (f-strings, modern class syntax).
- `views`/`pure` detection uses `stateMutability` instead of `visibility`.

### Fixed

- Python 3.13+ compatibility: generated parser code imported the removed
  `typing.io` module.
- Crashes: bare `delegatecall(data)`; `require()` without arguments in the
  tx.origin detector; a `payable(x)` cast in the arbitrary-call detector.
- Scanners no longer miss calls nested inside casts such as
  `uint8(sha3(...))` or `address(x)`.
- `Tools.scope_check` crashed on the same-line branch (attribute access on
  plain dicts) and compared the wrong columns.
- `get_below_statements` raised `KeyError` for nodes without a location.
- `VulTable`/`print_summary` crashed when every scanned file failed;
  `vul_count()` always returned 0.
- Compound pragmas (`^0.4.16 || ^0.5.0`) are now honoured by the integer
  overflow detector; `merge_loc_list([])` no longer raises.
- The `view`/`pure` guard in two detectors checked `visibility`, which caused
  false positives on view functions.
- Removed a hardcoded Etherscan API key from the legacy test suite
  (rotate it if it is still active).

### Removed

- `setup.py`, `requirements.txt` and the legacy `test.py` smoke tests.
